ordered_diagnoses: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the Trachea

facts.raw_span: 48-year-old white man
lifelong non-smoker
remote bronchoscopic resection of a tracheal carcinoid 17 years earlier
three-month history of mild hemoptysis
cough without dyspnea
non-tender, 2 × 2 cm subcutaneous mass on his left forearm
oxygen saturation of 94% on room air
normal laboratory studies, including complete blood count, liver and renal function tests, and coagulation profile
polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region adjacent to the anterior wall on chest CT scan
mass arising from the anterior tracheal wall just above the main carina, causing an 80% obstruction of the right main bronchus and 70% obstruction of the left main bronchus on flexible bronchoscopy
tumor consisted of large nests of eosinophilic cells within a collagenous and myxoid matrix on hematoxylin–eosin staining
carcinoid tumor was initially suspected

concepts.why: The patient has a history of a remote bronchoscopic resection of a tracheal carcinoid and presents with a polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region, which is consistent with a tracheal carcinoid tumor.
The patient presents with a mass arising from the anterior tracheal wall, causing obstruction of the main bronchi, which is consistent with a bronchial carcinoid tumor.
The patient presents with a polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region and a mass arising from the anterior tracheal wall, which could be consistent with a tracheal adenoid cystic carcinoma.

The patient presents with a polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region, which could be consistent with tracheal papillomatosis.
The patient presents with a three-month history of mild hemoptysis and cough, which could be consistent with an inflammatory tracheal polyp.
The patient presents with a three-month history of mild hemoptysis and cough, which could be consistent with a tracheal granuloma.
The patient presents with a mass arising from the anterior tracheal wall, causing obstruction of the main bronchi, which could be consistent with congenital tracheal stenosis.

rationales.F03: Previous history of tracheal carcinoid tumor increases the likelihood of another carcinoid tumor.
rationales.F10: The location and appearance of the mass are consistent with a tracheal or bronchial tumor.
rationales.F11: The histological description is consistent with a carcinoid tumor or other neuroendocrine tumor.
rationales.F12: The initial suspicion of a carcinoid tumor is based on the clinical and histological findings.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's history of remote bronchoscopic resection of a tracheal carcinoid 17 years earlier and the current presentation of a polypoid lesion in the precarinal tracheal region with hematoxylin–eosin staining showing large nests of eosinophilic cells support the diagnosis of Tracheal Carcinoid Tumor.
